data.name: Karunakar
data.gender_notes: Karunakar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Karunakar is a Sanskrit name derived from the words ‘karuna’ meaning compassion and ‘karan’ meaning the doer or controller. This name signifies a compassionate deity or a person who embodies compassion and mercy. The name Karunakar carries the meaning “Compassionate God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Karunakar usually hope their child will grow to embody compassionate god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Karunakar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Compassionate God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Karunakar total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Karunakara Varma was a Kerala ruler who ruled from 1555 to 1574 CE. He was a powerful monarch and expanded his kingdom through military conquests.
historical_references.context: The Chera Dynasty, also known as the Rajas of Venad or the Zamorins, was a ruling dynasty of Kerala in present-day India. Karunakara Varma was a Chera king who ruled during this period.

historical_references.reference: Karunakara Mutt was established in the 18th century by Saint Karunakara Guru. It is one of the five major mathas or monasteries of the Lingayat religion in Karnataka, India.
historical_references.context: Lingayatism is a religious tradition that originated in India during the 10th and 11th centuries CE. The Lingayat mathas are monastic institutions that serve as centers of learning, worship, and community organization for Lingayat followers.
